authoringPolicy: Only tag dimensions directly stated by the authored exercise instructions or success criterion. Omit unknown string, fret and position details; never infer them from a lesson title, skill name or generic exercise template.

topics.label: Standard tuning
topics.description: Name and tune the six standard open strings.

topics.label: TAB reading
topics.description: Translate authored tablature into string and fret actions.

topics.label: Open chord voicings
topics.description: Form and check the explicitly named open-position chord shapes.

topics.label: Eighth-note subdivision
topics.description: Maintain even eighth-note subdivisions and continuous strumming motion.

topics.label: Natural-note landmarks
topics.description: Locate natural notes using stated string and fret references.

topics.label: A minor pentatonic box 1
topics.description: Navigate the named A minor pentatonic box-1 pattern.

topics.label: Triad voicings
topics.description: Identify and play C, F and G triads on the named top three strings.

topics.label: Major-scale construction
topics.description: Play and name the C major note sequence and state the major-scale formula.

topics.label: A minor pentatonic note set
topics.description: Identify and use A–C–D–E–G without assuming a fretboard box or fingering.

topics.label: Melody transcription by ear
topics.description: Represent note order, interval movement and rhythm from a heard phrase.

topics.label: Triad inversions
topics.description: Play root position, first inversion and second inversion; identify the lowest chord tone.

topics.label: Rhythm transcription
topics.description: Capture beat grouping, attacks, accents and rests in a heard four-bar groove.

topics.label: Extended chord voicings
topics.description: Spell and play explicitly authored chord-extension shapes while controlling included and excluded strings.

techniques.label: Down-up strumming
techniques.description: Alternate downstrokes and upstrokes while preserving hand motion.

techniques.label: Alternate picking
techniques.description: Maintain a down-up pick sequence through a note cell.

techniques.label: String crossing
techniques.description: Plan and execute a picking-hand transition between adjacent strings.

techniques.label: Legato articulation
techniques.description: Use hammer-ons and pull-offs without re-picking every note.

techniques.label: Fingerstyle thumb independence
techniques.description: Maintain an even thumb-led bass pulse while treble fingers vary their pattern.

techniques.label: Target-pitch bending
techniques.description: Bend a fretted note toward an explicitly stated target pitch, then control its release.

techniques.label: P–I–M–A fingerstyle pattern
techniques.description: Play the prescribed thumb–index–middle–ring sequence across the explicitly named strings.

exerciseScopes.sourceEvidence: The exercise explicitly says to tune and play all six strings.
The exercise explicitly asks the learner to say each string and fret in a selected TAB phrase; no fixed string or fret range is authored.
The exercise names Em and G open-position shapes and requires a separate check of strings 6 through 1.
The exercise explicitly specifies eight down-up strokes, eighth-note counting and a skipped string contact.
The lesson explicitly scopes the parallel notation track to first-position notes on high E and B strings.
The exercise names low E and A strings and asks for natural notes within the first five frets, including open-string references.
The exercise explicitly specifies a D-U-D-U cell and a transition between two neighbouring strings; it does not name particular strings.
The exercise explicitly names A minor pentatonic box 1 and requires the shape to be played from low E to high E and back.
The lesson explicitly identifies the top three strings as G, B and high E and locates the C, F and G triad task there.
The musical-application exercise is explicitly a high-E legato cell and the checkpoint requires hammer-ons and pull-offs without re-picking.
The exercise explicitly assigns the low E bass note to the thumb and treble notes to i–m–a, then asks the learner to vary treble order without changing the bass pulse.
The exercise asks the learner to play and name one octave of C major, state A–C–D–E–G as A minor pentatonic and create a phrase ending on A; its success criterion includes the major-scale formula.
The exercise separates rhythm from pitch, locates the opening note from a reference, records interval movement and note order, then checks the independent transcription against the source.
The exercise plays root position, first inversion and second inversion, names the lowest chord tone in each and connects the voicings while retaining the triad quality.
The exercise claps the heard rhythm, writes attacks, accents and rests across four bars, then replays the groove to correct a timing or grouping error.
Exercise instruction: “G-D string answer melody (TAB core; staff optional).” Success criterion: “identify matching G- and D-string notes.”
Success criterion: “Read a short melody on strings 1-4 with rests and repeated notes.”
Exercise instruction: “Low E/A note map”. Success criterion: “Find and name every natural note to fret 5.” No lower fret bound is inferred.
Exercise instruction: “Fret B-string fret 8” and “Bend upward slowly until the pitch matches the fretted A at fret 10.”
Exercise instructions name D-string and G-string frets 5–7 with down-up-down-up strokes, then B-string frets 5–7–5–7 with hammer-ons and pull-offs.
Exercise instruction explicitly maps A minor pentatonic box 1: low E 5–8, A 5–7, D 5–7, G 5–7, B 5–8 and high E 5–8.
Exercise instructions explicitly require A minor pentatonic box 1, adjacent box 2, and connecting those two named positions. No string numbers or numeric fret range are stated.
Exercise instruction names C (x32010), Am (x02210) and the p–i–m–a sequence on strings 5–3–2–1.
Exercise instructions give Dm9 x5355xx, G13 3x345x and Cmaj9 x3243x, identify their chord extensions, and specify strings 5–2 and muted strings.
